content.text:
The request is valid and feasible, but I would narrow the contract before implementing it. The [discussion](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13109) currently has no replies.

### Findings

- `mise search` reads the static registry, with a special fallback for Aqua. There is no general backend catalog interface: [search.rs](/Users/jdx/src/mise/src/cli/search.rs:127).
- `mise use` without arguments also lists only static registry entries: [use.rs](/Users/jdx/src/mise/src/cli/use.rs:507).
- Tool-name completion runs `mise registry --complete`, which likewise emits only static registry entries: [mise-extra.usage.kdl](/Users/jdx/src/mise/src/assets/mise-extra.usage.kdl:48), [registry.rs](/Users/jdx/src/mise/src/cli/registry.rs:156).
- Vfox backend plugins expose only `BackendListVersions`, `BackendInstall`, and `BackendExecEnv`; all require an already-known tool name: [hooks.rs](/Users/jdx/src/mise/crates/vfox/src/lua_mod/hooks.rs:22), [backend_list_versions.rs](/Users/jdx/src/mise/crates/vfox/src/hooks/backend_list_versions.rs:6).
- A backend instance is itself tool-bound; it errors when the `plugin:tool` portion is absent: [vfox.rs](/Users/jdx/src/mise/src/backend/vfox.rs:582).

So this is a real missing capability, not a documentation problem.

### Recommended design

Add a vfox-specific optional hook, probably `BackendListTools`, while using a generic internal catalog record:

```lua
function PLUGIN:BackendListTools(ctx)
  return {
    tools = {
      { name = "prettier", description = "JavaScript formatter" },
      { name = "eslint", description = "JavaScript linter" },
    },
  }
end
```

Mise should construct the final identifiers as `plugin:name`. Plugins should not return arbitrary full backend identifiers or unprefixed aliases.

I would limit the first implementation to:

- Installed `VfoxBackend` plugins only.
- Optional `name` plus `description`.
- Nonfatal behavior when the hook is absent or fails.
- Validation and deduplication of returned names.
- Static registry entries taking precedence over duplicate results.
- No implicit addition to mise’s curated registry.

Internally, a shared `ToolCatalogEntry { id, description }` collector can feed search, completion, and selectors. That preserves room for another backend to implement discovery later without prematurely adding `list_tools` to every `Backend`.

### Important performance boundary

Do not execute arbitrary plugin/network code on every Tab press. Cache the catalog per plugin, invalidate it when the plugin source changes, and apply a timeout. Explicit discovery operations such as `mise search` and interactive `mise use` can refresh the catalog; completion should prefer cached/stale data.

This looks like a moderate, self-contained feature rather than a fundamental redesign. I made no repository changes.

You’re right. “Static” was the wrong distinction.

More accurately:

- The mise registry can be runtime-refreshed when `registry_floating` is enabled: [registry.rs](/Users/jdx/src/mise/src/registry.rs:34).
- Aqua registries can be downloaded/configured and cached: [aqua_registry_wrapper.rs](/Users/jdx/src/mise/src/aqua/aqua_registry_wrapper.rs:20).
- Shell completion runs `mise registry --complete` dynamically; it is not a generated fixed list.
- Only the default fallback snapshots are baked into the binary.

The real limitation is that discovery consumers currently draw from registry-shaped sources and do not merge catalogs supplied by installed backend plugins.

That changes my recommendation: a small general discovery-provider interface is probably appropriate, with adapters for:

1. The mise registry.
2. Aqua’s searchable catalog.
3. Optional `BackendListTools` hooks from vfox backend plugins.

It should still preserve `plugin:tool` namespacing and fast/offline cache behavior, but a vfox-only catalog bolted onto all three consumers would duplicate machinery that is already conceptually dynamic. The discussion’s suggestion of a “general backend discovery interface” is therefore stronger than I initially gave it credit for.

The user experience could look like this: ```toml [plugins] toolshed = "https://example.com/toolshed-plugin" ``` The plugin implements an optional catalog hook: ```lua function PLUGIN:BackendListTools(ctx) return { tools = { { name = "prettier", description = "JavaScript formatter", }, { name = "eslint", description = "JavaScript linter", }, }, } end ``` Mise adds the plugin prefix itself, producing `toolshed:prettier` and `toolshed:eslint`. ```mermaid flowchart LR R["Mise registry
possibly floating"] A["Aqua catalogs
configured or cached"] V["Installed backend plugins
BackendListTools"] C["Merged tool catalog
id + name + description + source"] S["mise search"] U["interactive mise use"] T["shell completion"] R --> C A --> C V --> C C --> S C --> U C --> T U --> X["Normal ToolArg resolution"] T --> X S -. selected/copied ID .-> X X --> LV["BackendListVersions(tool)"] LV --> I["Existing install flow"] ``` ### Commands Given the hook above: ```console $ mise search prettier Tool Description toolshed:prettier JavaScript formatter ``` ```console $ mise use toolshed: toolshed:eslint JavaScript linter toolshed:prettier JavaScript formatter ``` Running `mise use` without arguments would include those entries in its selector. After selection, everything proceeds normally: 1. `toolshed:prettier` is parsed as a `ToolArg`. 2. Mise resolves `toolshed` as an installed vfox backend plugin. 3. It calls `BackendListVersions` with `ctx.tool = "prettier"`. 4. The existing version selection and installation code takes over. No changes are needed to `BackendInstall` or `BackendExecEnv`. ### Internal shape I would not add `list_tools()` to the existing `Backend` trait. Backend instances are tied to a particular tool; the vfox implementation currently requires `plugin:tool`: [vfox.rs](/Users/jdx/src/mise/src/backend/vfox.rs:582). Instead, introduce a separate abstraction: ```rust struct ToolCatalogEntry { id: String, // "toolshed:prettier" name: String, // "prettier" description: Option, source: ToolCatalogSource, } trait ToolCatalogProvider { async fn list_tools( &self, policy: CatalogFetchPolicy, ) -> Result>; } ``` The existing mise registry, Aqua, and installed vfox backend plugins become providers. Search and selectors consume owned `ToolCatalogEntry` records instead of working directly with `&'static RegistryTool`. ### Fetch behavior Use two policies: - `FreshIfStale`: `mise search` and interactive `mise use` may execute the hook and refresh its cache. - `PreferCached`: shell completion uses cached results, with a short timeout on a cache miss. Catalogs should be cached per plugin and invalidated when: - The plugin is installed or updated. - Its Lua source changes. - The cache TTL expires. - The user clears that plugin’s cache. If refresh fails, mise should return stale entries when available. A broken or absent `BackendListTools` must not break normal installation. ### Scope and safety For the initial version: - Query only installed backend plugins; discovery should not install plugins implicitly. - Always namespace results under the installed plugin name. - Reject empty names and names containing syntax that would change the backend or version. - Do not inject plugin tools into `REGISTRY`; `mise registry` should retain its meaning. - Change completion to use an aggregate catalog command, perhaps hidden `mise search --complete`, rather than expanding `mise registry --complete`. - Allow only finite catalogs. Package-universe backends such as npm should continue using explicit identifiers rather than returning millions of packages. That gives backend plugins opt-in discovery without weakening registry curation or putting network calls directly into every completion attempt.
